news.title: Fifa World Cup plans: Governing body scraps Gianni Infantino's private investment proposal after widespread opposition
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino says he has scrapped the controversial plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's major competitions, following widespread opposition. Infantino said it had become clear the project had "created divisions" that are "no longer in the interest" of its original objective. The Swiss added: "As a result, this proposal will not proceed." Infantino had offered all 211 member associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups.

news.title: Infantino under huge pressure after plan for World Cup sell-off sparks resignation and rebuke
news.lede: Cordeiro quits as senior adviser to Fifa president. Lamour: sell-off plan ‘defies belief and imagination’. The walls started closing in on Gianni Infantino after another dramatic day that saw one of his senior advisers resign and brought a scathing rebuke from Fifa’s own chief operating officer. Infantino is under huge pressure after his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors met a tide of opposition from around the globe.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: Uprising at FIFA: Infantino faces the threat of removal by his closest ally, Mattias Grafström
news.lede: Gianni Infantino is facing the biggest challenge of his FIFA presidency after a controversial plan to introduce private investment into the World Cup’s commercial structure triggered a major backlash across global football. The FIFA president’s position has come under intense scrutiny, with former allies, governing bodies and political figures questioning whether he can continue leading the organization. The controversy centers on a reported proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise, a separate commercial entity that would oversee valuable FIFA assets, including broadcasting and sponsorship rights. The plan reportedly involves selling a 20% stake in the company, with the venture valued at around $20 billion.
